citeAs: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu (2021). Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning. ACL 2021.
creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu (UCLA, Zhejiang University, Sun Yat-sen University)
description: Geometry3K is a large-scale benchmark of 3,002 multi-choice high-school geometry problems collected from two textbooks, each annotated with dense formal language descriptions for both problem text and diagrams. The dataset covers diverse geometric shapes and problem goals (angle, length, area, ratio, etc.) and is divided into train (2,101), validation (300), and test (601) splits.
name: Geometry3K
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were well-trained individuals with undergraduate degrees. Human performance evaluation also involved dozens of graduates majoring in science or engineering as expert annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem (text, diagram, four choices, correct answer) and labeled each problem with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes. Additionally, each problem text and diagram was annotated with dense formal language descriptions using 91 defined predicates.
rai:dataCollection: Problems were collected from two popular high-school textbooks (grades 6-12) via two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline). Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry problems from two popular high-school textbooks (grades 6-12) accessed via two online digital libraries: McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline. Each raw problem includes problem text, a geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and a correct answer.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited in scale compared to general NLP datasets. The symbolic solver cannot handle complex problems with combined shapes and shaded areas. Diagram parsing fails on ambiguous annotations or multiple primitives. The text parser struggles with nested expressions and uncertain references. The theorem set is incomplete for some problem types.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each problem text and diagram was annotated with formal language descriptions using 91 defined predicates. Problems were labeled with problem goal type and geometry shape type. The dataset was split into train/validation/test sets at a 0.7:0.1:0.2 ratio.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset may inspire research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education. Problems are collected from online open sources.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking geometry problem solving algorithms, training and evaluating symbolic reasoning systems, interpretable math problem solving, and facilitating education research.
